method: Every visitor-facing field is split into exact contiguous segments. Each segment is counted by the recorded Unicode word matcher and marked source-derived or LAiDIES-authored. The sole Anthropic allocation includes conservative source-gap and provider-claim qualifications.

segments.text: Claude API prices are separate from subscription usage limits
segments.reason: Release subject and the API-price/subscription-limit distinction derive from the Anthropic announcement.

segments.text: Anthropic announced Claude Opus 5.5 on September 22.
For developers paying Anthropic directly for API use — a software connection to a model — input costs $4 and output $20 per million tokens.
segments.reason: API product boundary, plain definition and published token prices.

segments.text: Those are usage charges based on text processed, not monthly Claude subscription prices.
segments.reason: Necessary scope boundary for the published API prices.

segments.text: For subscriptions, Anthropic says it raised five-hour usage limits on Pro, Max, Team and seat-based Enterprise plans.
A usage limit is the amount a plan lets you use within a stated time window.
Subscription users also get a rate-limit reset they can save for later.
The announcement does not quantify those limits or map ordinary Claude-chat model-selector access plan by plan.
segments.reason: Bounded absence established by the complete source reread.

segments.text: “Available on all platforms” does not mean every account can select Opus 5.5 in chat today.
segments.reason: Conservative interpretation of the provider availability statement.

segments.text: If you pay for Claude chat, the API figures do not describe your monthly plan price.
segments.reason: Reader consequence of the API/subscription scope boundary.

segments.text: Check the model selector and current plan details for your account to see whether Opus 5.5 is offered and what limit applies.
segments.reason: LAiDIES action following from the unresolved account-specific gap.

segments.text: Anthropic says Opus 5.5 is best suited to moving a software project to a new system or reviewing its code.
For a simple email rewrite or summary, another Claude model may be a cheaper or faster alternative.
If you pay Anthropic directly for API usage, the token table is your meter.
segments.reason: Scoped reader consequence of the direct API prices.

segments.text: Anthropic’s performance, speed, safety and cost-per-task claims are not independently validated here.
segments.reason: Attribution and evidence-limit statement tied to the provider announcement.

segments.text: “Anthropic lowered API token prices and separately raised named subscriptions’ usage limits.
It did not publish each plan’s new limit or selector access.”
Working with AI 101 §7.4 — Free vs Paid (The Honest Answer) explains why the model, product surface and plan are separate choices — and why current access should be checked instead of remembered.
segments.reason: Governed LAiDIES learning link, not an Anthropic finding.
